purpose: Define three mandatory source-file header lines (deps, libs, target), with a single shared source of truth for code dependency declarations and platform compatibility. Enable target-safe Build Tool pruning and CW import.

scope.applies_to: Every AIGMos 1.9 source code file, INCLUDING Hardcore, Core Modules, System Lib, System Modules, EXPOSE implementations, AIGM User Modules and User Modules.
scope.excludes: No source-code category exemption; exceptions for shebang/encoding/generated code remain OPEN.
owns: target compatibility tag and its selection semantics

source_header.location: At the beginning of the source file, before imports and executable declarations.
source_header.value_format: deps/libs: JSON arrays of identifier strings; target: literal MP or CP

deps.meaning: Only the dependencies on modules and Hardcore interfaces used directly by this file.

libs.meaning: Only libraries, including System Lib, used directly by this file.

target.meaning: MP means compatible with both MicroPython and CPython. CP means CPython-only extended implementation.

declaration_rules: Both lines are always present, even when either or both lists are empty.
Only direct/immediate dependencies are declared; do not repeat indirect/transitive dependencies.
If a file uses a transitive dependency directly as well, declare that use explicitly.
deps and libs are separate and must not be interchanged.
Use stable dependency identifiers rather than filename/path inference.
Duplicate IDs or misclassified dependencies are errors.
No implicit authority or permission is granted by a declaration.
Every source file, including Hardcore files, declares all three headers; deps/libs may be empty.
target=MP is a compatibility claim for BOTH MP and CP. target=CP is a claim for CP only.
Never emit MP/CP as a value: use MP for shared code.
invalid_cases: MP-target source directly or transitively depending on CP-only code

examples.name: Empty valid header
examples.meaning: Either or both arrays may be empty.

examples.name: REST also using CS directly
examples.meaning: Direct CS use is declared even though EXP itself requires CS.

examples.name: CP-only extension
examples.meaning: Added functionality for CP only. No parallel duplicate of the shared MP implementation.

dependency_graph.collection: Read every source file once and extract all three fields with file provenance. Build typed direct-dependency graph and platform compatibility data in memory.
dependency_graph.resolution: Resolve IDs from the dependency registry and validate source classification and allowed dependency classes.
dependency_graph.closure: Compute transitive dependency closure after source collection; derived edges are not copied into source headers.
checks: transitive target eligibility for selected target MP/CP
prune unselected CP extensions even when build target is CP
dependency_graph.source_of_truth: The file header is the authority for declared code-level dependencies. Module manifest may include generated/validated dependency projections but must not duplicate independent, conflicting requires data.
dependency_graph.cw_import: CW importer may map direct typed edges with source-file provenance into StructureTree; it must mark closure edges derived rather than declared.

target_rules.build_target_MP: Only source files tagged MP and their MP-eligible transitive closure.
target_rules.build_target_CP: Source files tagged MP plus ONLY explicitly selected/required CP extensions and their closure.
target_rules.shared_implementation: MP is the single shared implementation; CP extends it rather than defining a second competing implementation.
target_rules.cs_interface: Same CS command syntax and semantics for both targets; unavailable capability returns an explicit failure when addressed.

pruning.confirmed: Build Tool removes every unneeded selected-feature component and exclusive dependency. NON-AC build removes AC implementation and its CS-hook code from the generated output.
pruning.unresolved: Exact pruning granularity and source-level conditional annotation syntax are not decided; do not assert arbitrary Python AST rewriting as locked.

architectural_classification.core_modules: Optional modules distinct from System Lib.
architectural_classification.system_lib: Reusable library code, a separate class from Core Modules and System Modules.
architectural_classification.exp: EXP is optional System Lib, directly dependent on HC.CS.
architectural_classification.rest: REST is an optional Expose module requiring EXP; a consumer need not repeat EXP's HC.CS dependency.
